Hi @apparao.puli@intel.com. I think it would be nice if you can split this out to separate patches for numeric sensor and numeric effecter. That would ease the review process a lot. However let's wait for the maintainer's opinions.

I started with that but over time, I ended up implementing both in single due to multiple dependencies across repo's and multiple commits (PLDM, PLDMtool etc). 

But small commits makes reviewer job easy but since it's all done now, Can we live with it for now?
Done
Can we use PLDM_EFFECTER_DATA_SIZE_MAX instead?
same as above
Please use LIBPLDM_ABI_TESTING instead. Read https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#abi-control

Since i started updating consumers also (https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/pldm/+/84666 & https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/pldm/+/84672) CI builds fail's for those. 

I am not fully aware of process and timeline for converting LIBPLDM_ABI_TESTING to LIBPLDM_ABI_STABLE. Can you please point me to more details if possible?

Anyway, for now i changed it.

Usually the APIs should be merged as TESTING first. Then, when there are patches with consumer codes to prove their implementation, we can have a patch to update TESTING -> STABLE and point to the consuming patches in the commit message.

As you are developing consuming code at the same time so I'm not sure. Maybe we should consult with the maintainer. For CI to pass, you can have a patch in between to do the the STABLE transition and set them all to the same topic for them to be built together.
Can this be something more adherent to the spec, like decode_numeric_sensor_state_sensor_event_data(). What do you think @andrew@codeconstruct.com.au?
With new struct, I renamed it to " and "decode_numeric_sensor_event_data" which is more appropriate. I think state sensors doesn't fir here.

Numeric Sensor State is the sensor event class name for this type of sensor event. You can see that there's a struct named `pldm_sensor_event_numeric_sensor_state`. So maybe this can be `decode_sensor_event_numeric_sensor_state_data()` as there's no such event named `numeric_sensor event` in the spec.

However, I don't know what the name of the struct your are adding should be as the name of the one you are replacing is already good.
This decode API is for Numeric Sensors event data decoding so name it that way - But this can be even be event_numeric_sensor . I feel either way is ok.

If there needs to be a new function, I would suggest adding a proper struct to hold the numeric sensor event data to follow the new convention https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#api-design.
Agree, Done
There's already a `pldm_msgbuf_extract_sensor_data()` in src/msgbuf/platform.h. I think you should enlist that function instead.
Good catch, Resolved
Can we use PLDM_EFFECTER_DATA_SIZE_MAX instead?
Same as above
This function takes uint8_t* for value, I don't understand why it can't support 64b.
Resolved now.
Can we use PLDM_EFFECTER_DATA_SIZE_MAX instead?
Same as above

There are two places consuming this function `decode_set_numeric_effecter_value_req` and `decode_get_numeric_effecter_value_resp`. `decode_get_numeric_effecter_value_resp` can totally be extended to 64b as the input param for value is uint8_t pointer.
 
The only issue left with using this extract function is from `decode_set_numeric_effecter_value_req`, which taking an input array of size 4 for the value. I wonder if we can update that function to extend the array size and update it consumers from pldm. As a result, this extract function can finally supports 64b.
Fixed

The commit message is for explaining why you're doing something, not what you've done. The patch itself tells us the latter.

If you find yourself writing a list of 15 things your patch does in the commit message this is a _strong sign_ that you should split your change up into constituent parts. Certainly for fixes like what you've listed here.
Agree, Done

@apuli@nvidia.com - I already have patches & was working on adding 64 bit numeric effecter support - can you please limit this review to only the sensor changes ? if you can review my patches and let me know what's missing I can add those at https://gerrit.openbmc.org/q/topic:%2264-bit-effecter-support%22

Hi Apparao, thanks for the change. I've listed a few concerns in comments inline.

Please no. Return an error. This is in the neighbourhood of a -5 on Rusty's API scale from ["What If I Don't Actually Like My Users?"](https://ozlabs.org/~rusty/index.cgi/tech/2008-04-01.html)

I recommend reading the complementary post [How Do I Make This Hard to Misuse?](https://ozlabs.org/~rusty/index.cgi/tech/2008-03-30.html) as well.
Agree, Anyway new API is defined to support it 64Bit - decode_numeric_sensor_event_data() - Done
As above.

https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/bf554b2a15505052e7f6803f8ff728465193a0b6/CONTRIBUTING.md#L344-L347

Done
Please drop all calls to `pldm_xlate_errno()` wrt to the comment about negative errno values above.
Done

`pldm_msgbuf_extract_p()` is an API that enables us to use the msgbuf abstractions to implement older APIs that deconstruct the message parameters as pointer arguments in library APIs.

That's not the case here though.

Please rather use:

```suggestion
	pldm_msgbuf_extract(buf, event_data->event_state);
```

and apply similar changes throughout where relevant.
Done
Done

I'd rather we clean this implementation up to use the msgbuf APIs than expand the approach that requires tedious analysis for spatial memory safety concerns.

Is that something you're willing to help with?
Done - https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/libpldm/+/86125
Done

Please fix throughout.
